feedback.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(5)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
